name: Improved Scalability for Large Sample Sizes via Dual Program

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $x\in\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\mathbb{X}^N$ and abbreviate
\[
    a_i \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} a_i(x),\qquad
    b_i \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} b_i(x),\qquad
    c \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} c(x),\qquad
    \tau \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} \tau(x),\qquad
    \theta_i \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} \theta_i(x),\qquad
    v_i \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} v_i(x).
\]
                                                                  
Since $s\ge2$ by the hypothesis of this proposition, one has
$\beta=s-1>0$. Moreover $M>0$, $R(x)>0$, and $\theta_i>0$ for every
$i\in[N]$. Consequently
\[
    c=\frac{s}{4MR(x)^{s-1}}>0,
    \qquad
    \tau=\beta MR(x)^{s+1}>0.
\]
For a function $\Xi:\mathbb{R}^k\to(-\infty,+\infty]$, where $k\in\mathbb N_+$, define its (convex) conjugate by 
\[
\Xi^*(u)\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\sup_{z\in\mathbb{R}^k} \{\langle u,z\rangle-\Xi(z)\}.
\]We compute the conjugates below and prove the equality of the optimal values by an explicit nonnegative gap. Since $b_i=a_i-c|v_i|^2$, the primal formula for $G$ becomes
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:dualization-primal-rewrite}
    G(x)
    =
    \min_{\lambda\in\Delta_N}
    \left\{
        \sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i b_i
        +
        c\left|\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i v_i\right|^2
        +
        \tau\operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\theta)
    \right\}.
\end{equation}
Define the linear map
$
    A:\mathbb{R}^N\to\mathbb{R}^d
$ by $A\lambda \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} \sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i v_i$ 
and define the extended-real-valued functions
\[
    \Phi(\lambda)
     \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} 
    \begin{cases}
        \displaystyle
        \sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i b_i
        +
        \tau\operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\theta),
        &\lambda\in\Delta_N,\\[2mm]
        +\infty,
        &\lambda\notin\Delta_N,
    \end{cases}
    \qquad
    \Psi(z) \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} c|z|^2.
\]
Then \eqref{eq:dualization-primal-rewrite} can thus be re-written as
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:dualization-composite-primal}
    G(x)
    =
    \min_{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^N}
    \bigl\{\Phi(\lambda)+\Psi(A\lambda)\bigr\}.
\end{equation}
The function $\Psi$ is finite, continuous and convex on $\mathbb{R}^d$.
The simplex $\Delta_N$ is nonempty, compact and convex, and
$t\mapsto t\log t$, with $0\log0 \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} 0$, is convex and continuous on
$[0,\infty)$. Hence $\Phi$ is proper, lower semicontinuous and convex.
The primal minimum is attained, since its objective is continuous on the nonempty compact simplex. We next compute the two conjugates directly. By definition,
$
    \Psi^*(y)
    =
    \sup_{z\in\mathbb{R}^d}
    \,
    \{\langle y,z\rangle-c|z|^2\}$.  
Completing the square,
$
    \langle y,z\rangle-c|z|^2
    =
    -c|z-\tfrac{y}{2c}|^2
    +
    \tfrac{|y|^2}{4c}
$; thus, for each $y\in\mathbb{R}^d$ we have
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:dualization-quadratic-conjugate}
    \Psi^*(y)=\frac{|y|^2}{4c}.
\end{equation}
Now let
$u=(u_i)_{i=1}^N\in\mathbb{R}^N$. Again by the definition of
the convex conjugate,
\[
\begin{aligned}
    \Phi^*(u)
    &=
    \sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_N}
    \left\{
        \sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i(u_i-b_i)
        -
        \tau\operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\theta)
    \right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Set
$
    Z(u)
     \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} 
    \sum_{i=1}^N
    \theta_i
    \exp\!\left(\frac{u_i-b_i}{\tau}\right)
    >0
$
and
$
    \pi_i(u)
     \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} 
    \tfrac{
        \theta_i\exp((u_i-b_i)/\tau)
    }{
        Z(u)
    }
$ for each $i\in[N]$.  
Then $\pi(u)\in\Delta_N^\circ$. Since
$
    \log\tfrac{\pi_i(u)}{\theta_i}
    =
    \tfrac{u_i-b_i}{\tau}
    -
    \log Z(u)$ 
for every $\lambda\in\Delta_N$ we have
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:dualization-entropy-identity}
\begin{aligned}
    \sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i(u_i-b_i)
    -
    \tau\operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\theta)
    &=
    \tau\log Z(u)
    -
    \tau\operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\pi(u)).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
For completeness,
$\operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\pi(u))\ge0$. Indeed,
$\log r\le r-1$ for $r>0$, and hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
    -\operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\pi(u))
=
    \sum_{\lambda_i>0}
    \lambda_i
    \log\frac{\pi_i(u)}{\lambda_i}
\le
    \sum_{\lambda_i>0}
    \lambda_i
    \left(
        \frac{\pi_i(u)}{\lambda_i}-1
    \right)
=
    \sum_{\lambda_i>0}\pi_i(u)-1
    \le 0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Equality holds at $\lambda=\pi(u)$. Thus
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:dualization-entropy-conjugate}
    \Phi^*(u)
    =
    \tau
    \log\!\left(
        \sum_{i=1}^N
        \theta_i
        \exp\!\left(
            \frac{u_i-b_i}{\tau}
        \right)
    \right).
\end{equation}
Retain the fixed point $x$ and the coefficients introduced above. Throughout the following argument these coefficients are held fixed; in particular, $c>0$, $\tau>0$, $b_i\in\mathbb{R}$, $v_i\in\mathbb{R}^d$, and $\theta_i>0$ with $\sum_{i=1}^N\theta_i=1$. Recall that
    \[
     A\lambda=\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i v_i,\qquad \Psi(z)=c|z|^2,\qquad \Phi(\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i b_i+\tau\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i\log\frac{\lambda_i}{\theta_i}\quad(\lambda\in\Delta_N),
    \]
    where each summand with $\lambda_i=0$ is interpreted as zero. The spaces $\mathbb{R}^N$ and $\mathbb{R}^d$ are equipped with their Euclidean inner products. Hence, for every $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^N$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
    \[
     \langle A\lambda,y\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i\langle v_i,y\rangle=\left\langle\lambda,\bigl(\langle y,v_i\rangle\bigr)_{i=1}^N\right\rangle.
    \]
    By the defining property of the adjoint, this proves $(A^*y)_i=\langle y,v_i\rangle$ for every $i\in[N]$.  For $y\in\mathbb{R}^d$, put
    $
     \mathcal Z(y)\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\sum_{i=1}^N\theta_i\exp\!\left(-\frac{b_i+\langle y,v_i\rangle}{\tau}\right)$.
    Every summand is finite and strictly positive. Consequently, $\mathcal Z(y)>0$, and the previously defined Gibbs vector $\pi(-A^*y)$ has coordinates
    \[
     \pi_i(-A^*y)=\frac{\theta_i\exp\!\left(-\frac{b_i+\langle y,v_i\rangle}{\tau}\right)}{\mathcal Z(y)},\qquad i\in[N].
    \]
    In particular, $\pi_i(-A^*y)>0$ for every $i$, and summing the numerators gives $\sum_{i=1}^N\pi_i(-A^*y)=1$. Thus $\pi(-A^*y)\in\Delta_N^\circ$.  Define the dual objective by
    $
     \mathcal D(y)\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}-\Phi^*(-A^*y)-\Psi^*(y)$ for $y\in\mathbb{R}^d$.  
    The computed formula for $\Phi^*$ and \eqref{eq:dualization-quadratic-conjugate} give
    \[
     \Phi^*(-A^*y)=\tau\log\mathcal Z(y),\qquad \mathcal D(y)=-\tau\log\mathcal Z(y)-\frac{|y|^2}{4c}.
    \]
    Since $\mathcal Z$ is a finite sum of smooth, strictly positive functions, $\mathcal D$ is finite and smooth on $\mathbb{R}^d$.
    
    We next establish the gap identity, including its validity on the boundary of the simplex. First, the non-negativity of relative entropy can be seen directly from the function
    $
     \varphi(t)\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} t\log t-t+1$ for each $t>0$ and $\varphi(0)\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}1$; and not that the extension at zero is continuous (since $\lim_{t\downarrow0}t\log t=0$). 
     For $t>0$, one has $\varphi'(t)=\log t$; thus $\varphi$ decreases on $(0,1)$ and increases on $(1,\infty)$. It follows that $\varphi(t)\ge0$ for every $t\ge0$, with equality precisely when $t=1$. For $\lambda\in\Delta_N$, the positivity of the Gibbs coordinates therefore gives
    \[
     \operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\pi(-A^*y))=\sum_{i=1}^N\pi_i(-A^*y)\varphi\!\left(\frac{\lambda_i}{\pi_i(-A^*y)}\right)\ge0.
    \]
    Indeed, expanding the sum on the right gives the relative entropy plus $-\sum_i\lambda_i+\sum_i\pi_i(-A^*y)$, and these last two terms cancel. This calculation uses the convention $0\log(0/a)=0$ for $a>0$, so it includes zero coordinates of $\lambda$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $\lambda=\pi(-A^*y)$.  Taking logarithms gives
    $
     \log\pi_i(-A^*y)=\log\theta_i-\frac{b_i+\langle y,v_i\rangle}{\tau}-\log\mathcal Z(y)$. 
    For each index with $\lambda_i>0$, substitute this expression into $\lambda_i\log(\lambda_i/\pi_i(-A^*y))$. Indices with $\lambda_i=0$ contribute zero throughout. Summing and using $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$, we obtain
    \[
     \begin{aligned}
     \tau\operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\pi(-A^*y))
     &=\tau\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i\log\frac{\lambda_i}{\theta_i}+\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i\bigl(b_i+\langle y,v_i\rangle\bigr)+\tau\log\mathcal Z(y)\\
     &=\Phi(\lambda)+\langle y,A\lambda\rangle+\Phi^*(-A^*y).
     \end{aligned}
    \]
    This is \eqref{eq:dualization-entropy-identity} evaluated at $u=-A^*y$. Rearranging it and using $\Psi(A\lambda)=c|A\lambda|^2$ yields
    \[
     \begin{aligned}
     \Phi(\lambda)+\Psi(A\lambda)-\mathcal D(y)
     &=\Phi(\lambda)+c|A\lambda|^2+\Phi^*(-A^*y)+\frac{|y|^2}{4c}\\
     &=\tau\operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\pi(-A^*y))+c|A\lambda|^2-\langle y,A\lambda\rangle+\frac{|y|^2}{4c}.
     \end{aligned}
    \]
    Completing the square in the last three terms proves that, for every $\lambda\in\Delta_N$ and $y\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
    \begin{equation}
    \label{eq:dualization-direct-gap}
     \Phi(\lambda)+\Psi(A\lambda)-\mathcal D(y)=c\left|A\lambda-\frac{y}{2c}\right|^2+\tau\operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\pi(-A^*y))\ge0.
    \end{equation}
    
    The restriction of $\Phi+\Psi\circ A$ to $\Delta_N$ is continuous: the only boundary terms requiring attention are $\lambda_i\log\lambda_i$, and these extend continuously by zero at $\lambda_i=0$. Since $\Delta_N$ is nonempty and compact, its minimum is finite and attained. By \eqref{eq:dualization-composite-primal}, this minimum equals $G(x)$. Taking the minimum over $\lambda\in\Delta_N$ in \eqref{eq:dualization-direct-gap} therefore gives
    \[
     \mathcal D(y)\le\min_{\lambda\in\Delta_N}\{\Phi(\lambda)+\Psi(A\lambda)\}=G(x)
    \]
     for each $y\in\mathbb{R}^d$.  
    We now prove that the dual supremum is attained. Since $N\ge1$, the first summand in $\mathcal Z(y)$ gives
    $
     \mathcal Z(y)\ge\theta_1\,e^{-\frac{b_1+\langle y,v_1\rangle}{\tau}}.
    $
    The logarithm is increasing and $\tau>0$. Hence
    \[
     \begin{aligned}
     \mathcal D(y)\le-\frac{|y|^2}{4c}+b_1+\langle y,v_1\rangle-\tau\log\theta_1\le-\frac{|y|^2}{4c}+|v_1||y|+b_1-\tau\log\theta_1.
     \end{aligned}
    \]
    Because $c>0$, the quadratic term dominates the linear term as $|y|\to\infty$. Consequently, $\mathcal D(y)\to-\infty$ as $|y|\to\infty$. In particular, there exists $R>0$ such that
    if $
     |y|\ge R$ then $\mathcal D(y)<\mathcal D(0)-1$.  
    The continuous function $\mathcal D$ attains its maximum on the compact ball $\overline B(0,R)$ at some point $y_*$. Since $0\in\overline B(0,R)$, one has $\mathcal D(y_*)\ge\mathcal D(0)$. Every point outside that ball has strictly smaller value. Thus $y_*$ is a global maximizer of $\mathcal D$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$.
    
    It remains to show that this maximizer yields equality in \eqref{eq:dualization-direct-gap}. Term-wise differentiation is legitimate because the defining sum for $\mathcal Z$ is finite, and gives
    $
     \nabla\mathcal Z(y)=-\frac1\tau\sum_{i=1}^N\theta_i\,e^{-\frac{b_i+\langle y,v_i\rangle}{\tau}}v_i$.   Since $\mathcal Z(y)>0$, the chain rule now yields
    \[
     \begin{aligned}
     \nabla\mathcal D(y)=-\frac{y}{2c}-\tau\frac{\nabla\mathcal Z(y)}{\mathcal Z(y)}=-\frac{y}{2c}+\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{\theta_i\exp\!\left(-\frac{b_i+\langle y,v_i\rangle}{\tau}\right)}{\mathcal Z(y)}\,v_i=-\frac{y}{2c}+A\pi(-A^*y).
     \end{aligned}
    \]
    For each $h\in\mathbb{R}^d$, the differentiable function $t\mapsto\mathcal D(y_*+th)$ has a global maximum at $t=0$. Its derivative there is therefore zero, so $\langle\nabla\mathcal D(y_*),h\rangle=0$ for every $h$. Consequently $\nabla\mathcal D(y_*)=0$.
      
    Set $\lambda_*\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\pi(-A^*y_*)$. The positivity and normalization already proved give $\lambda_*\in\Delta_N^\circ$, and the gradient identity implies
    $
     A\lambda_*=\tfrac{y_*}{2c}$.  
    Thus the squared term in \eqref{eq:dualization-direct-gap} vanishes at $(\lambda_*,y_*)$. The relative-entropy term also vanishes, since $\lambda_*=\pi(-A^*y_*)$. It follows that
    \[
    \Phi(\lambda_*)+\Psi(A\lambda_*)=\mathcal D(y_*)
    .
    \]
    Combining this equality with the previously established bound $\mathcal D(y_*)\le G(x)$ and the admissibility of $\lambda_*$ gives
    \[
     \mathcal D(y_*)\le G(x)\le\Phi(\lambda_*)+\Psi(A\lambda_*)=\mathcal D(y_*).
    \]
    Every inequality is therefore an equality. In particular, $\lambda_*$ attains the primal minimum, $y_*$ attains the dual maximum, and their values coincide:
    \begin{equation}
    \label{eq:dualization-fenchel-rockafellar}
     G(x)=\max_{y\in\mathbb{R}^d}\{-\Phi^*(-A^*y)-\Psi^*(y)\}.
    \end{equation}
Substituting $u=-A^*y$ into
\eqref{eq:dualization-entropy-conjugate} and using
\eqref{eq:dualization-quadratic-conjugate} therefore yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
    G(x)
    &=
    \max_{y\in\mathbb{R}^d}
    \Biggl\{
        -\frac{|y|^2}{4c}
        -
        \tau
        \log\!\Biggl(
            \sum_{i=1}^N
            \theta_i
            \exp\!\left(
                -\frac{
                    b_i+\langle y,v_i\rangle
                }{\tau}
            \right)
        \Biggr)
    \Biggr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Restoring the $x$-dependence gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
    G(x)
=
    \max_{y\in\mathbb{R}^d}
    \Biggl\{
        -\frac{|y|^2}{4c(x)}
        -
        \tau(x)
        \log\!\Biggl(
            \sum_{i=1}^N
            \theta_i(x)
            \exp\!\left(
                -\frac{
                    b_i(x)+\langle y,v_i(x)\rangle
                }{\tau(x)}
            \right)
        \Biggr)
    \Biggr\}
=
    F(x)
,
\end{aligned}
\]
where the last equality is exactly
\eqref{eq:entropy-variance-extension}.
Finally, if $x=X_n$ for some $n\in[N]$, the prescribed on-site
definitions give $
    G(X_n)=P_n(X_n)=F(X_n)$.  
Thus $G(x)=F(x)$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$.

body_md:

name: real-analyticity Away from the Measurement Sites

label: eq:offsite-analytic-objective
title: Proof
body_md:
Put $U\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\mathbb X^N$ and retain $r_i(x)=|x-X_i|$. For every $t\in\mathbb{R}$ and each $x\in U$
\[
 r_i(x)^t=\exp\!\left(\frac t2\log\!\left(\sum_{k=1}^d(x_k-X_{i,k})^2\right)\right)
 .
\]
Consequently all the powers of $r_i$ used in the reconstruction are real-analytic on $U$. Since $\mu_i>0$, one has
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^N\mu_jr_j^{-q}>0,\qquad \theta_i>0,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^N\theta_i=1,\qquad R^p=\sum_{i=1}^N\theta_i r_i^p>0.
\]
The formulas defining $\theta_i$, the positive root $R$, and $v_i$ therefore give real-analytic functions on $U$; here each $P_i$ is a polynomial. Retain $a_i,b_i,c,\tau$ from~\eqref{eq:gibbs-dual-quantities}. They are real-analytic on $U$, and $c,\tau>0$ because $M,R>0$ and $\beta=s-1\ge1$.
\hfill\\
\noindent
For $x\in U$ and $\lambda\in\Delta_N$, set
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:offsite-analytic-objective}
 \begin{aligned}
 m_\lambda(x)&\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i v_i(x),\\
 \mathcal J(x,\lambda)&\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i b_i(x)+c(x)|m_\lambda(x)|^2+\tau(x)\operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\theta(x)).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Specializing~\eqref{eq:entropy-variance-extension__primal} to $\vartheta=1$ and expanding the variance, then using $b_i=a_i-c|v_i|^2$, gives $F(x)=\min_{\lambda\in\Delta_N}\mathcal J(x,\lambda)$. For each fixed $x$, apply Lemma~\ref{lem:three-entropy} to $\mathcal J(x,\lambda)/\tau(x)$, with scalar costs $b_i(x)/\tau(x)$, vectors $v_i(x)$, weights $\theta_i(x)$, and quadratic coefficient $c(x)/\tau(x)>0$. Its existence, boundary-variation, and strict-convexity arguments give a unique minimizer $\lambda^*(x)\in\Delta_N^\circ$. Write $z_*(x)\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} m_{\lambda^*(x)}(x)$. The Gibbs identity in that lemma yields
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:offsite-analytic-gibbs}
 \begin{aligned}
 Z(x,z)&\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\sum_{i=1}^N\theta_i(x)\exp\!\left(-\frac{b_i(x)+2c(x)\langle z,v_i(x)\rangle}{\tau(x)}\right)>0,\\
 \pi_i(x,z)&\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\frac{\theta_i(x)\exp\!\left(-\frac{b_i(x)+2c(x)\langle z,v_i(x)\rangle}{\tau(x)}\right)}{Z(x,z)},\\
 \bar v(x,z)&\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\sum_{i=1}^N\pi_i(x,z)v_i(x),\qquad H(x,z)\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} z-\bar v(x,z),\\
 \lambda_i^*(x)&=\pi_i(x,z_*(x)),\qquad H(x,z_*(x))=0.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The functions $Z$, $\pi_i$, $\bar v$, and $H$ are jointly real-analytic on $U\times\mathbb{R}^d$, and $\pi(x,z)\in\Delta_N^\circ$.
Now, every zero of $H(x,\cdot)$ determines the actual minimizer. Indeed, substitution of
\[
 \log\frac{\pi_i(x,z)}{\theta_i(x)}=-\frac{b_i(x)+2c(x)\langle z,v_i(x)\rangle}{\tau(x)}-\log Z(x,z)
\]
into~\eqref{eq:offsite-analytic-objective} gives, for every $\lambda\in\Delta_N$, we have
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:offsite-analytic-gap}
 \mathcal J(x,\lambda)=-c(x)|z|^2-\tau(x)\log Z(x,z)+c(x)|m_\lambda(x)-z|^2+\tau(x)\operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\pi(x,z)).
\end{equation}
This identity includes zero coordinates of $\lambda$, with $0\log(0/b)=0$ for $b>0$. If $H(x,z)=0$, then $m_{\pi(x,z)}(x)=z$, and hence
\[
 \mathcal J(x,\lambda)-\mathcal J(x,\pi(x,z))=c(x)|m_\lambda(x)-z|^2+\tau(x)\operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\pi(x,z))\ge0.
\]
For the last inequality, $u\log(u/v)\ge u-v$ for $u\ge0$, $v>0$; summing over two probability vectors gives non-negativity of relative entropy. Uniqueness of the minimizer therefore proves that: if $H(x,z)=0$ then $\pi(x,z)=\lambda^*(x)$, $ z=z_*(x)$.
Differentiating the finite sums with respect to $z$, for $u\in\mathbb{R}^d$, gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D_z\log Z(x,z)[u]&=-\frac{2c(x)}{\tau(x)}\langle\bar v(x,z),u\rangle,\\
 D_z\pi_i(x,z)[u]&=-\frac{2c(x)}{\tau(x)}\pi_i(x,z)\langle v_i(x)-\bar v(x,z),u\rangle,\\
 D_zH(x,z)&=I+\frac{2c(x)}{\tau(x)}\sum_{i=1}^N\pi_i(x,z)(v_i(x)-\bar v(x,z))\otimes(v_i(x)-\bar v(x,z)).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here $(a\otimes b)u\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\langle b,u\rangle a$. Thus
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:offsite-analytic-jacobian}
 \langle D_zH(x,z)u,u\rangle=|u|^2+\frac{2c(x)}{\tau(x)}\sum_{i=1}^N\pi_i(x,z)\langle v_i(x)-\bar v(x,z),u\rangle^2\ge|u|^2.
\end{equation}
Consequently $D_zH(x,z)$ has trivial kernel and is invertible.

Fix $x_0\in U$, put $z_0=z_*(x_0)$, and let $B=D_zH(x_0,z_0)$. We give the analytic implicit-function step directly. The real-analytic map
\[
 T(\xi,w)\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} w-B^{-1}H(x_0+\xi,z_0+w)
\]
satisfies $T(0,0)=0$ and $D_wT(0,0)=0$. Write its power series as $T(\xi,w)=\sum_{\alpha,\eta\in\mathbb N^d}t_{\alpha\eta}\xi^\alpha w^\eta$, with $t_{\alpha\eta}\in\mathbb{R}^d$, and choose convergence radii $a_0,b_0>0$ such that
\[
 \sum_{\alpha,\eta}|t_{\alpha\eta}|_\infty a_0^{|\alpha|}b_0^{|\eta|}<\infty.
\]
Here $|w|_\infty\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\max_j|w_j|$, $t_{00}=0$, and $t_{0,e_j}=0$ for each coordinate vector $e_j$. Choose $0<b<b_0/2$ and then $0<a<a_0$ such that $x_0+[-a,a]^d\subset U$ and
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:offsite-analytic-radii}
 A(a)\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\sum_\alpha|t_{\alpha0}|_\infty a^{|\alpha|}\le\frac b2,\qquad Q(a,b)\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\sum_{\alpha,\,|\eta|\ge1}|\eta|\,|t_{\alpha\eta}|_\infty a^{|\alpha|}b^{|\eta|-1}\le\frac12.
\end{equation}
Indeed, $|\eta|(b/b_0)^{|\eta|-1}\le1$ when $|\eta|\ge1$ and $b<b_0/2$, so the series defining $Q(a,b)$ is dominated by $b_0^{-1}\sum_{\alpha,\eta}|t_{\alpha\eta}|_\infty a_0^{|\alpha|}b_0^{|\eta|}$. Its part with $\alpha=0$ tends to zero as $b\downarrow0$, since $t_{0,e_j}=0$; choose $b$ so that this part is at most $1/4$. Holding $b$ fixed and decreasing $a$, the part with $|\alpha|\ge1$ becomes at most $1/4$, while $A(a)\le b/2$ because $t_{00}=0$. These choices may also be made with $a<\rho_{\mathbb X^N}(x_0)/(2\sqrt d)$, which ensures the stated inclusion in $U$.

Let $\mathcal A_a$ be the space of scalar power series $g(\xi)=\sum_\alpha g_\alpha\xi^\alpha$ with $\|g\|_a\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\sum_\alpha|g_\alpha|a^{|\alpha|}<\infty$. It is complete, being a weighted $\ell^1$ space, and coefficient convolution gives $\|gh\|_a\le\|g\|_a\|h\|_a$. On $\mathcal A_a^d$ use $\|g\|_{a,\infty}\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\max_j\|g_j\|_a$. For $\|g\|_{a,\infty},\|h\|_{a,\infty}\le b$, telescoping each monomial gives
\[
 \|g^\eta-h^\eta\|_a\le|\eta|b^{|\eta|-1}\|g-h\|_{a,\infty}\qquad(|\eta|\ge1).
\]
Consequently the substitution $\mathcal T(g)(\xi)\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} T(\xi,g(\xi))$ is well defined and satisfies
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\mathcal T(g)-\mathcal T(h)\|_{a,\infty}&\le Q(a,b)\|g-h\|_{a,\infty}\le\tfrac12\|g-h\|_{a,\infty},\\
 \|\mathcal T(g)\|_{a,\infty}&\le A(a)+\tfrac12\|g\|_{a,\infty}\le b.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Starting from $g^{(0)}=0$, the iterates $g^{(k+1)}=\mathcal T(g^{(k)})$ satisfy
\[
 \|g^{(k+1)}-g^{(k)}\|_{a,\infty}\le2^{-k}\frac b2.
\]
They therefore converge in $\mathcal A_a^d$ to a fixed point $g$. Since $T(0,0)=0$, every iterate vanishes at zero, and hence $g(0)=0$. Every scalar $h=\sum_\alpha h_\alpha\xi^\alpha\in\mathcal A_a$ is real-analytic on $(-a,a)^d$: for $\xi_0\in(-a,a)^d$ and $0<\rho<a-|\xi_0|_\infty$, its binomial re-expansion about $\xi_0$ is absolutely convergent, bounded by $\sum_\alpha|h_\alpha|(|\xi_0|_\infty+\rho)^{|\alpha|}\le\|h\|_a$. Hence $\zeta(x)\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} z_0+g(x-x_0)$ is real-analytic on $V\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} x_0+(-a,a)^d$ and satisfies $\zeta(x_0)=z_0$ and $H(x,\zeta(x))=0$. 
Since we knew that: if $H(x,z)=0$ then $\pi(x,z)=\lambda^*(x),\qquad z=z_*(x)$; then we deduce that $\zeta(x)=z_*(x)$ on $V$; no prior continuity of the minimizer is required.
  
Evaluating~\eqref{eq:offsite-analytic-gap} at $z=z_*(x)$ and $\lambda=\lambda^*(x)$ now gives: for every $x\in V$
\[
 F(x)=-c(x)|z_*(x)|^2-\tau(x)\log Z(x,z_*(x)).
\]
The right-hand side is real-analytic, since all its constituents are real-analytic on $V$ and $Z>0$. Since $x_0\in U$ was arbitrary and $V$ is a neighborhood of $x_0$ contained in $U$, it follows that $F\in C^\omega(U)$.

head: environment
name: Definability of the Reconstruction

title: Proof
body_md:
We retain the notation of $\S$\ref{s:TheFormula} and~\eqref{eq:three-aux-geometry}; definability below uses only the parameters in the statement. Since $d,N,s$ are fixed, \eqref{eq:fancy_constants} gives $\beta\in\mathbb N$, $p\in\mathbb N_+$, $q=p+46d+2\in\mathbb N_+$, and $A_s\in\mathbb Q$. Moreover,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 x\notin\mathbb X^N&\quad\mbox{ if and only if } \quad\bigwedge_{i=1}^N\left(\sum_{k=1}^d(x_k-X_{i,k})^2>0\right),\\
 \lambda\in\Delta_N&\quad\mbox{ if and only if } \quad\left(\bigwedge_{i=1}^N\lambda_i\ge0\right)\land\left(\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i=1\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus both domains are definable. For $x\notin\mathbb X^N$ and $i\in[N]$, the relations
\[
\begin{aligned}
 r_i(x)=a&\quad\mbox{ if and only if } \quad a>0\ \land\ a^2=\sum_{k=1}^d(x_k-X_{i,k})^2,\\
 b=a^{-1}&\quad\mbox{ if and only if } \quad ab=1\qquad(a>0)
\end{aligned}
\]
give definable distances and positive reciprocals. Hence $S_q$ is definable, and
\[
 S_q(x)>0,\qquad \theta_i(x)>0,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^N\theta_i(x)=1,\qquad R(x)^p=\sum_{i=1}^N\theta_i(x)r_i(x)^p>0.
\]
In particular,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \theta_i(x)=a&\quad\mbox{ if and only if } \quad aS_q(x)=\mu_i r_i(x)^{-q},\\
 R(x)=a&\quad\mbox{ if and only if } \quad a>0\ \land\ a^p=\sum_{i=1}^N\theta_i(x)r_i(x)^p.
\end{aligned}
\]
These identities make $\theta_i$ and $R$ definable. The components of $\nabla P_i$ are polynomials in $x$ with coefficients obtained from those of $P_i$ by multiplication by integers. Thus $v_i$ is definable as well. Here each integer power is fixed, and compositions are expressed by real quantifiers over intermediate values. When $s=0$, $\nabla P_i=0$ and $v_i(x)=Mr_i(x)^{-1}(x-X_i)$; the reciprocal is defined because $r_i(x)>0$.

For $a>0$, $\log a=b$ is equivalent to $\exp(b)=a$. With the entropy convention in $\S$\ref{s:Notation}, the graph of its scalar summand is therefore
\[
 \left\{(t,u,z)\in\mathbb R^3:\ u>0\ \land\
 \left[\begin{array}{l}
 (t=0\land z=0)\ \lor{}\\
 \bigl(t>0\land\exists w\in\mathbb R:\ u\exp(w)=t\land z=tw\bigr)
 \end{array}\right]\right\}.
\]
For $u>0$ and $0<t\le1$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |t\log(t/u)|
 &\le -t\log t+t|\log u|
 =t\int_t^1\frac{\mathrm d a}{a}+t|\log u|\\
 &\le t\int_t^1 a^{-3/2}\,\mathrm d a+t|\log u|
 =2\sqrt t-2t+t|\log u|
                                 
\end{aligned}
\]
the right-hand side of which converges to $0$ as $t$ tends to $0$ from the right.
Consequently, $\lambda\mapsto\operatorname{KL}(\lambda\mid\theta(x))$ is finite and continuous on all of $\Delta_N$ for each $x\notin\mathbb X^N$.

Let $\mathcal E_1(x,\lambda)$ denote the objective in~\eqref{eq:entropy-variance-extension__primal} specialized to $\vartheta=1$. By~\eqref{eq:weighted_variance}, the variance is polynomial in $\lambda$ and the coordinates of $v_i$. Since $M,R(x)>0$, the preceding identities imply that $\mathcal E_1:(\mathbb R^d\setminus\mathbb X^N)\times\Delta_N\to\mathbb R$ is definable and  $
 \mathcal E_1(x,\cdot)\in C(\Delta_N)$.  
In particular, at $s=0$ the variance denominator is $4M/R(x)>0$, whereas at $s=1$ it is $4M>0$; the entropy is finite before multiplication by $\beta=0$ in either case.

Fix $x\notin\mathbb X^N$. For any sequence $(\lambda^k)_{k\ge1}\subseteq\Delta_N$, successive dyadic subdivisions of $[0,1]^N$ give nested closed cubes $Q_j$ of side length $2^{-j}$ containing infinitely many sequence terms. Choose $k_j\uparrow\infty$ with $\lambda^{k_j}\in Q_j$. For $\ell\ge j$, $|\lambda^{k_\ell}-\lambda^{k_j}|\le\sqrt N\,2^{-j}$; hence 
\[
 \lim\limits_{j\uparrow \infty} \, \lambda^{k_j} =\bar\lambda,\qquad
 \bar\lambda_i=\lim_{j\to\infty}\lambda_i^{k_j}\ge0,\qquad
 \sum_{i=1}^N\bar\lambda_i=\lim_{j\to\infty}\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i^{k_j}=1.
\]
Thus $\bar\lambda\in\Delta_N$. Put $a_x\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\inf_{\lambda\in\Delta_N}\mathcal E_1(x,\lambda)$. Nonemptiness of $\Delta_N$ and finiteness of $\mathcal E_1$ give $a_x<+\infty$. If $a_x=-\infty$, choose $\mathcal E_1(x,\lambda^k)\le-k$ and extract the preceding subsequence. Continuity would give both $\mathcal E_1(x,\lambda^{k_j})\to\mathcal E_1(x,\bar\lambda)\in\mathbb R$ and $\mathcal E_1(x,\lambda^{k_j})\le-k_j\to-\infty$, a contradiction. Hence $a_x\in\mathbb R$. Choose $0\le\mathcal E_1(x,\lambda^k)-a_x\le k^{-1}$ and extract $\lambda^{k_j}\to\lambda^*\in\Delta_N$. Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
 0\le\mathcal E_1(x,\lambda^*)-a_x
 &=\lim_{j\to\infty}\bigl(\mathcal E_1(x,\lambda^{k_j})-a_x\bigr)
 \le\lim_{j\to\infty}k_j^{-1}=0,\\
 F(x)&=\mathcal E_1(x,\lambda^*)=a_x.
\end{aligned}
\]

Let $G_{\mathcal E_1}(x,\lambda,t)$ be the definable graph relation for $\mathcal E_1$ obtained above. For $(x,t)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:reconstruction-definable-offsite-graph}
\begin{aligned}
 &(x,t)\in\operatorname{graph}\!\left(F|_{\mathbb R^d\setminus\mathbb X^N}\right)\\
 &\quad\mbox{ if and only if } \quad x\notin\mathbb X^N\ \land\ \exists\lambda\in\mathbb R^N\,\Bigl[
 \lambda\in\Delta_N\land G_{\mathcal E_1}(x,\lambda,t)\\
 &\qquad\land\ \forall(\eta,z)\in\mathbb R^N\times\mathbb R,\
 \bigl([\eta\in\Delta_N\land G_{\mathcal E_1}(x,\eta,z)]\Longrightarrow z\ge t\bigr)\Bigr].
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
For the forward implication, take $\lambda=\lambda^*$. Conversely, the quantified conditions give $\mathcal E_1(x,\lambda)=t\le\mathcal E_1(x,\eta)$ for every $\eta\in\Delta_N$, hence $t=F(x)$. The simplex constraints and $G_{\mathcal E_1}$ are finite first-order formulas; hence so is the right-hand side of~\eqref{eq:reconstruction-definable-offsite-graph}. Finally,~\eqref{eq:entropy-variance-extension__primal___SITES} gives
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:reconstruction-definable-global-graph}
 \operatorname{graph}(F)=\operatorname{graph}\!\left(F|_{\mathbb R^d\setminus\mathbb X^N}\right)
 \cup\bigcup_{i=1}^N\{(X_i,P_i(X_i))\}.
\end{equation}
Each added singleton has defining formula $\bigwedge_{k=1}^d(x_k=X_{i,k})\land(t=P_i(X_i))$, using the same parameters. Finite disjunction proves global definability. The argument also applies to $\Delta_1=\{(1)\}$, coincident polynomial jets at distinct sites, and vanishing coordinates of a minimizer; it uses neither uniqueness of $\lambda^*$ nor definability of $f$.

name: Gradients and Lipschitz Constants

title: Proof
body_md:
If $B \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} \sup_\Omega|\nabla u|<\infty$, the segment joining $x,y\in\Omega$ lies in $\Omega$. The one-variable fundamental theorem of calculus applied to $t\mapsto u(x+t(y-x))$ gives
\[
 u(y)-u(x)=\int_0^1\nabla u(x+t(y-x))\cdot(y-x)\,\mathrm d t,
 \qquad |u(y)-u(x)|\le B|y-x|.
\]
Hence $\operatorname{Lip}_\Omega(u)\le B$; this inequality is automatic if $B=\infty$. Conversely, if $L_u \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} \operatorname{Lip}_\Omega(u)<\infty$, each $x\in\Omega$ and unit vector $\xi$ satisfy $x+t\xi\in\Omega$ for all sufficiently small $|t|$, because $\Omega$ is open. Therefore
\[
 |\nabla u(x)\cdot\xi|
 =\left|\lim_{t\to0}\frac{u(x+t\xi)-u(x)}{t}\right|\le L_u.
\]
For a nonzero gradient choose its own unit direction; for a zero gradient the norm is zero. Taking the supremum proves $B\le L_u$, and if $L_u=\infty$ this inequality is automatic. This proves the equality, including its infinite cases. Under the last hypothesis the continuous gradient is bounded on the compact closure, which makes $B$ finite; the segment estimate then makes $L_u$ finite.

Fix an input satisfying Data Format~\ref{dataformat}. Put $U=\mathbb R^d\setminus\{X_1,\ldots,X_N\}$ and $H=F_{\operatorname{ext}}|_U$. Every constant denoted by $C$ below is absolute and may increase between occurrences. We first verify the emitted scalar graph, then its decorated adjacency representation, and finally the work of its uniform implementation.

\emph{1. Emission and realization.}

Write $\widetilde V_0=\{\mathbf x_1,\ldots,\mathbf x_d\}$, $\widetilde V_t=\widetilde V_0\sqcup\{v_1,\ldots,v_t\}$, $c(\mathbf x_j)=j$, and $c(v_t)=d+t$, where $v_t$ is the $t$th emitted vertex. For an instantiation with distinct supplied handles $(u_j)_{j=1}^m$ and formal computation vertices $(a_k)_{k=1}^L$, the substitution table satisfies
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sigma(\text{port}_j)&=u_j\qquad(j\in[m]),\\
\sigma(a_k)&\notin\widetilde V_{\rm before}\sqcup\{\sigma(a_\ell):\ell<k\}\qquad(k\in[L]),\\
\sigma(a_k)&\ne\sigma(\text{port}_j)\qquad(k\in[L],\ j\in[m]).
\end{aligned}
\]
For $k,\ell\in[L]$, $\sigma(a_k)=\sigma(a_\ell)$ if and only if $k=\ell$; for $i,j\in[m]$, $\sigma(\text{port}_i)=\sigma(\text{port}_j)$ if and only if $i=j$. The supplied tuples belong to $\{\boldsymbol x,\boldsymbol y,(\boldsymbol x,\chi),(u_1,\ldots,u_N,\boldsymbol y)\}$. Freshness in the coordinate and site iterations gives $y_j\ne y_k$ for distinct $j,k\in[d]$ and $u_i\ne u_k$ for distinct $i,k\in[N]$. Moreover,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\max_{j\in[d]}c(\mathbf x_j)&<c(\chi)<\min_{j\in[d]}c(y_j)\le\max_{j\in[d]}c(y_j)<\min_{i\in[N]}c(u_i).
\end{aligned}
\]
In a reduction, its leaf handles are distinct and every internal handle is fresh. Hence $T[j]\ne T[k]$ for distinct allocated positions $j,k$, in particular $T[2j]\ne T[2j+1]$. A repeated monomial operand $u$ is replaced by the three fresh vertices $z=\operatorname{New}(\mathsf c_0;u)$, $u'=\operatorname{New}(+_2;u,z)$, and $\operatorname{New}(\times_2;u,u')$, with $u\ne z$ and $u\ne u'$. Every remaining binary call in the emitter definitions has a fresh-constant pair, a distinct-monomial pair, a division pair treated below, or one of the following pairs of handles from distinct branches:
\[
\begin{gathered}

\end{aligned}
\]
The $N=1$ branch is $\operatorname{Inst}(\theta;\boldsymbol v)=\operatorname{New}(\mathsf c_1;v_1)$, so $G_\theta=1$ in that case. Parameter reads, handle reads and writes, and loop updates have bounded instruction counts per displayed operation; $N+d\le2Nd$ gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{|\cdot-X_i|}+W_{I_{\cdot=X_i}}+W_{S_a}&\le Cd,\\
W_\theta&\le N W_{|\cdot-X_i|}+W_{\rho_{+_2},N}+C(N+d)\le CNd,\\
W_R&\le W_\theta+N W_{|\cdot-X_i|}+W_{\rho_{+_2},N}+C(N+d)\le CNd,\\
W_{E_{\operatorname{exp}}}&\le W_R+N W_{|\cdot-X_i|}+C(N+d)\le CNd.
\end{aligned}
\]

The algorithm contains $2N$ polynomial reductions, $N$ indicator reductions, at most $6N$ distance reductions, at most seven further $N$-input reductions, and one $(N+1)$-input reduction. Consequently, if $\mathcal R$ is the multiset of reduction calls and $m_R$ is the input count of call $R$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{R\in\mathcal R}m_R&\le2NB+7Nd+8N+1\le2NB+16Nd,\\
\sum_{R\in\mathcal R}2\bar m_R&<4\sum_{R\in\mathcal R}m_R\le8NB+64Nd,\\
W_{\text{initializing all reduction arrays}}&\le C\sum_{R\in\mathcal R}m_R\le C(NB+Nd),
\\
K&\le d+16NB+4Nd+17Nd+31Nd+55Nd+5d+11N+13\\
&\le16NB+140Nd.
\end{aligned}
\]

Including input records and the computation of $a$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{\rm emit}&\le Cd+W_a+2N W_{\operatorname{Poly}}+\sum_{i=1}^N W_{I_{\cdot=X_i}}+W_{S_a}+W_\theta+W_{E_{\operatorname{exp}}}+W_R\\
&\quad+2W_{\rho_{+_2},N}+W_{\rho_{+_2},N+1}+CN\\
&\le C\bigl(N(B+d)+Nd+N+d\bigr)\le C(NB+Nd),\qquad W_a\le C(N+d).
\end{aligned}
\]

Relative to the maximum depth of their formal inputs, the constructor depth recurrences are
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_\delta&\le2+3+\tau_d+1=6+\tau_d,&D_I&\le1+\tau_d,&D_{S_a}&\le4,\\
D_{\operatorname{Poly}}&\le2+3h_s+1+\tau_B=3h_s+\tau_B+3,\\
D_\theta&\le\begin{cases}1,&N=1,\\D_\delta+4+\tau_N,&N\ge2,\end{cases}\\
D_R&\le\max\{D_\theta,D_\delta+1\}+\tau_N+2\le D_\delta+6+2\tau_N,\\
D_{E_{\operatorname{exp}}}&\le\max\{D_R,D_\delta\}+7\le D_\delta+13+2\tau_N.
\end{aligned}
\]
For the master circuit, with $D_p=D_{\operatorname{Poly}}$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_\chi&\le D_I+\tau_N+2,\qquad D_y\le D_\chi+4,\\
D_t&\le1+\max\{D_I,D_p\},\qquad D_u\le D_y+D_p,\\
D_\eta&\le D_y+D_\theta,\qquad D_r\le D_y+D_R,\\
D_e&\le D_u+D_{E_{\operatorname{exp}}},\\
D_\ell&\le1+\tau_N+1+\max\{D_\eta,D_e\},\qquad D_k\le D_r+2,\\
D_h&\le1+\max\{D_\ell,D_k\},\\
D_{\rm out}&\le\tau_{N+1}+\max\{D_t,1+\max\{D_\chi,D_h\}\}\\
&\le33+3h_s+\tau_B+2\tau_d+4\tau_N+\tau_{N+1}\\
&\le42+3h_s+h_B+2h_d+5h_N\le C_s\log_2(d+N).
\end{aligned}
\]
The last bound uses $B\le(s+1)d^s$, $h_B\le1+\log_2(s+1)+s\log_2d$, $h_d,h_N\le1+\log_2(d+N)$, and $\log_2(d+N)\ge1$.

\emph{4. Uniform implementation and final bounds.}

Put $L=B+d+1$, $H_0=NL$, and $K_0=160H_0$. The finite template dependencies are
\[
E_{\operatorname{exp}}\longrightarrow R\longrightarrow\theta\longrightarrow\operatorname{Dist}\longrightarrow\rho_{+_2},
\qquad \operatorname{Poly}\longrightarrow\rho_{+_2},
\qquad I_{\cdot=X_i}\longrightarrow\rho_{\times_2}.
\]
They give at most $J=8$ simultaneously active table-bearing frames, including the compiler frame. The bounds on formal ports, reduction heaps, and emitted vertices are
\[
\begin{aligned}
m_{\rm ports}&\le\max\{N+d+1,B\}\le H_0,\qquad K\le K_0,\\
m_\rho&\le\max\{B,d,N+1\}\le H_0,\qquad 2\bar m_\rho<4H_0.
\end{aligned}
\]
For a table-bearing call $F$, let $m_F$ be its port count and $L_F$ the number of vertices emitted during the call, including nested calls. Returned handles are retained before a child table is reused; only scalar counters are reset between calls. Copying each fresh handle to the currently active tables gives
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:compiler-table-work}
\begin{aligned}
\sum_Fm_F&\le d+2Nd+Nd+(d+1)+3d+2d+(N+d)+6Nd\\
&\quad +(2NB+7Nd+8N+1)\\
&=2NB+16Nd+8d+9N+2\le2NB+35Nd,\\
\sum_FL_F&=\sum_{v\notin\widetilde V_{\rm in}}
\#\{F:F\text{ is active when }v\text{ is emitted}\}\le8(K-d),\\
W_{\rm tables}&\le C\sum_F(m_F+L_F)\le C(2NB+35Nd+8K)\le C(NB+Nd).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
These sums include the compiler frame and all reduction calls.

For a table-bearing call $F$, let $c_F$ be the vertex count at entry, let $\zeta_F$ be its word-table base, and let $(u_{F,j})_{j=1}^{m_F}$ be its supplied handles. Store $\sigma_F[j]$ at address $\zeta_F+j-1$ as the word $c(\sigma_F[j])$. The port copies and active-table appends are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf W[\zeta_F+j-1]&\gets c(u_{F,j}) &&(1\le j\le m_F),\\
\mathsf W[\zeta_G+m_G+c(v)-c_G-1]&\gets c(v) &&(G\text{ active when }v\text{ is emitted}).
\end{aligned}
\]
For a formal operand index $0\le\xi<m_F+c(v)-c_F$ used when emitting $v$, the word passed to the constructor is $1=c(\mathbf x_1)$ if $\xi=0$, and is read from $\mathsf W[\zeta_F+\xi-1]$ otherwise. In the latter case, $1\le\xi\le m_F+c(v)-c_F-1$, so the accessed entry is a supplied port or a previously appended handle. There are $\sum_Fm_F$ port writes, $\sum_FL_F$ append writes, and at most $2(K-d)$ operand reads. A returned tuple has at most $m_F+L_F$ handles, copied before table reuse. Since the compiler frame contributes $L_F=K-d$, all these reads, writes, address computations, and loop updates are included in $W_{\rm tables}\le C\sum_F(m_F+L_F)$ from~\eqref{eq:compiler-table-work}.

The safe point and real gate labels require only the permitted exact-real operations. With $A_0=1$, compute
\[
A_i=A_{i-1}+\begin{cases}X_{i,1},&X_{i,1}\ge0,\\-X_{i,1},&X_{i,1}<0,\end{cases}
\qquad
a_j=\begin{cases}A_N,&j=1,\\0,&2\le j\le d,\end{cases}
\qquad q_{\mathbb R}=\operatorname{embed}(q).
\]
This costs $W_a\le C(N+d)$. Every subsequently emitted real gate parameter belongs to
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:compiler-parameters}
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_0&=\{0,1,-1,q,2s,s+1,\tfrac12,\tfrac1{2s},\tfrac1{1-s},A_s,M,(1-s)M\},\\
\mathcal L&=\mathcal L_0\cup\{X_{i,j},-X_{i,j},\mu_i,c_{i,\alpha},a_j,-a_j:i\in[N],\ j\in[d],\ \alpha\in\Lambda\},\\
W_{\lambda(v)}&\le C.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The program loads fixed rational literals, reads supplied real data, and forms these labels using $+,-,\times$, sign tests, and the single word embedding. Thus the compiler records power, exponential, and logarithm gates without evaluating those functions. Setting $D=2^{q-2s-2}\ge1$ gives $2s+\lceil\log_2D\rceil+2=q$, identifying the instance of Theorem~\ref{thrm:complexity}; the compiler does not evaluate $D$.

Lemma~\ref{lem:compiler-ram-implementation} implements these exact emissions and scans by a finite program $\mathcal P_{d,s}$ independent of $N,q,w$. Its hypotheses follow from the preceding bounds and~\eqref{eq:compiler-parameters}. Under~\eqref{eq:compiler-word-capacity}, it gives $W_{\rm init}\le CH_0$, the table-maintenance bound in~\eqref{eq:compiler-table-work}, and $W_{\rm scan}\le CK$, with every intermediate word value strictly below $2^w$. An admissible word length is
\[
w=\left\lceil\log_2\bigl(q+C_{\rm mem}(d,s)(N+1)+1\bigr)\right\rceil
=\mathcal O_{d,s}\bigl(\log(q+N)\bigr).
\]

Initialization consists of actual memory writes. Use the blocks $J_{\nu,t}$, bases $b_{\nu,t}$, and lengths $n_{\nu,t}$ in~\eqref{eq:compiler-ram-layout}. Before emission, load $\mathsf W[2]\gets0$, $\mathsf W[3]\gets1$, and $\mathsf R[2]\gets0$. For each block, set $\mathsf W[0]\gets b_{\nu,t}$ and $\mathsf W[1]\gets b_{\nu,t}+n_{\nu,t}$; while $\mathsf W[0]<\mathsf W[1]$, execute
\[
\begin{cases}\mathsf W[\mathsf W[0]]\gets\mathsf W[2],&\nu=\mathbb W,\\\mathsf R[\mathsf W[0]]\gets\mathsf R[2],&\nu=\mathbb R,\end{cases}\qquad\mathsf W[0]\gets\mathsf W[0]+\mathsf W[3].
\]
After $j$ iterations the pointer equals $b_{\nu,t}+j$, and the first $j$ block cells have been zeroed. Thus there are exactly $n_{\nu,t}$ writes, with no iteration for an empty block. The disjointness in~\eqref{eq:compiler-ram-layout} preserves the input and register cells; Lemma~\ref{lem:compiler-ram-implementation} supplies the capacity bound for the addresses and loop endpoints. Including the fixed number of block-base calculations, comparisons, increments, and scratch-register initializations gives $W_{\rm init}\le C(1+\sum_{\nu,t}n_{\nu,t})\le CH_0$.

Since $d\le B=\prod_{j=1}^s(d+j)/j\le\prod_{j=1}^sd(j+1)/j=(s+1)d^s$ and $B+d+1\le(s+3)d^s$, the vertex and edge counts are
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:compiler-vertex-edge-count}
K\le16NB+140Nd\le C_sNd^s,\qquad
|\widetilde E|=\sum_{v\notin\widetilde V_{\rm in}}\operatorname{ar}(g_v)\le2(K-d).
\end{equation}
The implementation estimates give
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:compiler-work}
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Work}(\texttt{Compile-Circuit})
&\le W_{\rm init}+W_{\rm emit}+W_{\rm tables}+W_{\rm scan}\\
&\le CN(B+d+1)\le C_sNd^s.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The designated output consists of $4K+2$ word cells and $K$ real cells, so
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:compiler-output-storage}
\operatorname{OutputStorage}(\texttt{Compile-Circuit})=5K+2\le C_sNd^s.
\end{equation}
Finally,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{dom}(f_{\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\operatorname{ext}},I_d})&=\Omega_{K-d}=\mathbb R^d,
&f_{\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\operatorname{ext}},I_d}&=F_{\operatorname{ext}},\\
|\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\operatorname{ext}}|&=K-d\le C_sNd^s,
&\operatorname{width}(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\operatorname{ext}})&\le K\le C_sNd^s,\\
\operatorname{depth}(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\operatorname{ext}})&\le C_s\log_2(d+N).
\end{aligned}
\]
  
With the inputs available at time $0$, evaluate each computation vertex $v\in\widehat V\setminus[d]$ at time $\widehat D(v)$. If $(u,v)\in\widehat E$, then the depth recurrence gives $\widehat D(u)\le\widehat D(v)-1$. If $v\in\widehat V\setminus[d]$, then $1\le\widehat D(v)\le D_{\rm out}$, since every vertex reaches $\iota(v_{\rm out})$. Moreover,
\[
\#\{v\in\widehat V\setminus[d]:\widehat D(v)=t\}\le K-d\le C_sNd^s\qquad(t\in[D_{\rm out}]).
\]
Induction on $t$ therefore evaluates every gate scheduled at time $t$ from operands available by time $t-1$. This schedule uses at most $K-d$ ideal processors and $D_{\rm out}\le C_s\log_2(d+N)$ unit-time steps.

label: eq:compiler-ram-input
title: Proof
body_md:
Throughout the proof, $C$ denotes an absolute constant which may increase between occurrences. We set $r_*=512$ and use the polynomial emitter's coefficient order $\Lambda=\{\alpha^{(0)},\ldots,\alpha^{(B-1)}\}$. The input encoding is
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:compiler-ram-input}
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf W[r_*]&=N,&\mathsf W[r_*+1]&=q,&\mathsf R[r_*]&=M,\\
\mathfrak a(i,\ell)&=r_*+1+(i-1)L+\ell &&&(i\in[N],\ 0\le\ell<L),\\
\mathsf R[\mathfrak a(i,j-1)]&=X_{i,j} &&&(j\in[d]),\\
\mathsf R[\mathfrak a(i,d)]&=\mu_i,\\
\mathsf R[\mathfrak a(i,d+1+k)]&=c_{i,\alpha^{(k)}} &&&(0\le k<B),\\
\mathfrak a(i,0)+L&=\mathfrak a(i+1,0) &&&(i<N),\\
\mathfrak a(N,L-1)&=r_*+NL,&n_{\mathbb R}^{\rm in}&=1+H_0,&n_{\mathbb W}^{\rm in}&=2.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
For $\mathsf W[0]=a$, $\mathsf W[1]=b$, and $\mathsf W[2]=c$, where $a,b\ge r_*$ and $c\ge r_*+1+H_0$, real arithmetic is implemented by
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf R[0]&\gets\mathsf R[\mathsf W[0]],&\mathsf R[1]&\gets\mathsf R[\mathsf W[1]],\\
\mathsf R[2]&\gets\mathsf R[0]\circ\mathsf R[1],&\mathsf R[\mathsf W[2]]&\gets\mathsf R[2],\qquad\circ\in\{+,-,\times\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For $m\ge1$, put $\bar m=2^{\lceil\log_2m\rceil}$. The hypotheses give
\[
\begin{gathered}
m_F\le\max\{N+d+1,B\}\le H_0,\qquad L_F\le K\le K_0,\\
m_\rho\le\max\{B,d,N+1\}\le H_0,\qquad 2\bar m_\rho<4H_0.
\end{gathered}
\]
In each memory, we reserve the disjoint register banks
\[
\begin{gathered}
\mathcal B_{\rm pr}=[0,32)\cap\mathbb N_0,\qquad\mathcal B_{\rm gl}=[32,64)\cap\mathbb N_0,\\
\mathcal B_\ell=[64+32\ell,96+32\ell)\cap\mathbb N_0\qquad(0\le\ell<8),\\
\mathcal B_{\rm pr}\sqcup\mathcal B_{\rm gl}\sqcup\bigsqcup_{\ell=0}^7\mathcal B_\ell=[0,320)\cap\mathbb N_0\subset[0,r_*),\\
n_{\rm pr}\le4\ \text{fields}+6\ \text{addresses}+6\ \text{operands}=16<32,\\
n_{\rm gl}^{\mathbb W}\le14\ \text{block bases}+10\ \text{counters}+4\ \text{pointers}=28<32,\\
n_{\rm local}\le3\ \text{indices}+5\ \text{pointers}+12\ \text{handles}+4\ \text{offsets}=24<32,\\
\mathsf R[32]=q_{\mathbb R},\qquad \mathsf R[33]=M,\qquad \mathsf R[34]=(1-s)M,\qquad \mathsf R[35]=A_i.
\end{gathered}
\]
Here $A_i=1+\sum_{k=1}^i|X_{k,1}|$. A call at depth $\ell$ uses $\mathcal B_\ell$; indexed families remain in arrays. The twelve local handles of $E_{\operatorname{exp}}$ are $(r,r^{-1},p_R,p_M,p_M^{-1},\delta_i,a_i,\beta_i,b_i,c_i,d_i,e_i)$. Arithmetic uses $\mathcal B_{\rm pr}$; only the initial embedding writes $\mathsf R[32]$.

Write $c(v)$ for the creation index, including the $d$ inputs. For each table-bearing call $F$, let $c_F$ be the vertex count at entry, $(u_{F,j})_{j=1}^{m_F}$ its supplied handles, and $\zeta_F$ its word-table base. Put $\mathfrak s_F(j)=\zeta_F+j-1$. For the innermost active call $F$, execute
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:compiler-ram-tables}
\begin{aligned}
\sigma_F[j]&\gets u_{F,j} &&(1\le j\le m_F),\\
\sigma_F^*(a)&=\begin{cases}\mathbf x_1,&a=0,\\\sigma_F[a],&a\ge1,\end{cases}\\
v&\gets\operatorname{New}\bigl(g;\sigma_F^*(a_1),\ldots,\sigma_F^*(a_{\operatorname{ar}(g)})\bigr),\\
0\le a_j&<m_F+c(v)-c_F &&(j\in[\operatorname{ar}(g)]),\\
\sigma_G[m_G+c(v)-c_G]&\gets v &&(G\text{ active}),\\
1\le c(v)-c_G&\le L_G,\qquad m_G+L_G\le H_0+K_0.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
If $a_j=0$ for an operand index, then $g=\mathsf c_z$ for some $z\in\mathbb R$. Handles are stored as their creation indices:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf W[\mathfrak s_F(j)]&\gets c(u_{F,j}) &&(1\le j\le m_F),\\
h_j&\gets\begin{cases}1,&a_j=0,\\\mathsf W[\mathfrak s_F(a_j)],&a_j\ge1,\end{cases} &&(1\le j\le\operatorname{ar}(g)),\\
\mathsf W[\mathfrak s_G(m_G+c(v)-c_G)]&\gets c(v) &&(G\text{ active}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Each $h_j$ occupies a word register. If $a_j=0$, then the load is $1=c(\mathbf x_1)$ and no table cell is accessed. If $a_j\ge1$, then $a_j\le m_F+c(v)-c_F-1$, so the read lies among the ports or previously appended entries. Copy each returned tuple once before table reuse; it has at most $m_F+L_F$ handles. The compiler frame has $L_F=K-d$, and hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_{\rm tables}&\le C\left(\sum_Fm_F+\sum_FL_F+2(K-d)+\sum_F(m_F+L_F)\right)\\
&\le C\sum_F(m_F+L_F).
\end{aligned}
\]
The four terms count port writes, active-table appends, operand reads, and return copies; $C$ includes address calculations and loop updates. Only scalar counters are reset between calls. Inlining the finite acyclic call graph at its syntactic call sites gives literal jump targets and requires no return stack. Polynomial splitting ranks and coefficient offsets are fixed literals for $d,s$.

We allocate the following blocks after the input, reusing the eight template tables by call depth and the heap after each reduction:
\[
\begin{array}{c|r|r}
\text{block}&\text{word cells}&\text{real cells}\\\hline
\text{temporary records}&4K_0&K_0\\
\text{relabelling map}&K_0&0\\
\text{reserved output}&4K_0+2&K_0\\
\text{retained handles and safe point}&7N+d+8&d\\
\text{template tables}&8(K_0+H_0)&0\\
\text{monomial table}&B&0\\
\text{reduction heap}&4H_0&0
\end{array}
\]
The retained tuples are $(b_i)_i,(p_i)_i,(t_i)_i,(u_i)_i,(\eta_i)_i,(e_i)_i,(w_i)_i,(y_j)_j$; the eight further slots hold $r_0,\chi,r,\ell,k,h,\chi h,v_{\rm out}$. For the entry $n_{\nu,t}$ in row $t$ and column $\nu\in\{\mathbb W,\mathbb R\}$, set
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:compiler-ram-layout}
\begin{aligned}
\beta_{\mathbb W}&=r_*+2,\qquad\beta_{\mathbb R}=r_*+1+H_0,\\
b_{\nu,t}&=\beta_\nu+\sum_{j=1}^{t-1}n_{\nu,j},\\
J_{\nu,t}&=[b_{\nu,t},b_{\nu,t}+n_{\nu,t})\cap\mathbb N_0,\\
J_{\nu,t}\cap J_{\nu,t'}&=\varnothing\quad(t\ne t'),\qquad J_{\nu,t}\cap[0,\beta_\nu)=\varnothing,\\
n_{\mathbb W}^{\rm all}&=514+17K_0+12H_0+7N+d+B+10\le3265H_0,\\
n_{\mathbb R}^{\rm all}&=513+H_0+2K_0+d\le835H_0,\\
W_{\rm init}&\le C\sum_{\nu,t}n_{\nu,t}\le CH_0.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Before emission, load $\mathsf W[2]\gets0$, $\mathsf W[3]\gets1$, and $\mathsf R[2]\gets0$. For each block $J_{\nu,t}$, set $\mathsf W[0]\gets b_{\nu,t}$ and $\mathsf W[1]\gets b_{\nu,t}+n_{\nu,t}$. While $\mathsf W[0]<\mathsf W[1]$, execute
\[
\begin{cases}\mathsf W[\mathsf W[0]]\gets\mathsf W[2],&\nu=\mathbb W,\\\mathsf R[\mathsf W[0]]\gets\mathsf R[2],&\nu=\mathbb R,\end{cases}\qquad\mathsf W[0]\gets\mathsf W[0]+\mathsf W[3].
\]
After $j$ iterations, for $0\le j\le n_{\nu,t}$, the pointer is $b_{\nu,t}+j$ and the first $j$ block cells are zero. Thus the loop makes exactly $n_{\nu,t}$ writes; if $n_{\nu,t}=0$, then it makes none. By~\eqref{eq:compiler-ram-layout}, the written blocks exclude the input and registers. Including block-base calculations, register initialization, comparisons, and increments gives $W_{\rm init}\le C(1+\sum_{\nu,t}n_{\nu,t})\le CH_0$.

Let $b_{\mathbb W}^{\rm tmp},b_{\mathbb R}^{\rm tmp}$ and $b_{\mathbb W}^{\rm out},b_{\mathbb R}^{\rm out}$ be the temporary and output record bases, and let $\zeta_\iota$ be the relabelling-map base. For $v$ with creation index $k=c(v)$ and ordered parents $(u_j)_{j=1}^{\operatorname{ar}(v)}$, put $\pi_j(v)=c(u_j)$ if $j\le\operatorname{ar}(v)$ and $\pi_j(v)=0$ otherwise, for $j\in\{1,2\}$. Append the record by
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf W[b_{\mathbb W}^{\rm tmp}+4(k-1)]&\gets\operatorname{tag}(v),\\
\mathsf W[b_{\mathbb W}^{\rm tmp}+4(k-1)+1]&\gets\operatorname{ar}(v),\\
\mathsf W[b_{\mathbb W}^{\rm tmp}+4(k-1)+1+j]&\gets\pi_j(v)\qquad(j\in\{1,2\}),\\
\mathsf R[b_{\mathbb R}^{\rm tmp}+k-1]&\gets\lambda(v).
\end{aligned}
\]
For distinct fixed scratch addresses $a,b\in\mathcal B_{\rm pr}$, use the indirect reads and writes
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf W[b]&\gets\mathsf W[\mathsf W[a]],&\mathsf W[\mathsf W[a]]&\gets\mathsf W[b],\\
\mathsf R[b]&\gets\mathsf R[\mathsf W[a]],&\mathsf R[\mathsf W[a]]&\gets\mathsf R[b].
\end{aligned}
\]
Memory-to-memory copies pass through a scratch register. Each record append writes four word fields and one real field. These writes, affine address calculations, and the counter update cost at most $C$ instructions per append and are charged to $W_{\rm emit}$.

The first scan initializes $n_{\rm c}\gets0$ and counts constant tags in $\mathsf W[b_{\mathbb W}^{\rm tmp}+4(k-1)]$, $k\in[K]$. The second reads the tags, computes the ranks from Step~2 of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thrm:complexity__Assembly}, and writes $\mathsf W[\zeta_\iota+c(v)-1]\gets\iota(v)$. The third reads each temporary record's four word fields and one real field and obtains
\[
\begin{aligned}
\ell&\gets\mathsf W[\zeta_\iota+c(v)-1],\\
\rho_j&\gets\begin{cases}\mathsf W[\zeta_\iota+\pi_j(v)-1],&j\le\operatorname{ar}(v),\\0,&j>\operatorname{ar}(v),\end{cases}\qquad j\in\{1,2\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
If $\operatorname{ar}(v)=2$, then one comparison gives $(p_1(v),p_2(v))=(\min\{\rho_1,\rho_2\},\max\{\rho_1,\rho_2\})$; otherwise $(p_1(v),p_2(v))=(\rho_1,\rho_2)$. Put $(f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3)=(\operatorname{tag}(v),\operatorname{ar}(v),p_1(v),p_2(v))$ and write
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf W[b_{\mathbb W}^{\rm out}+2+4(\ell-1)+j]&\gets f_j\qquad(0\le j\le3),\\
\mathsf R[b_{\mathbb R}^{\rm out}+\ell-1]&\gets\mathsf R[b_{\mathbb R}^{\rm tmp}+c(v)-1].
\end{aligned}
\]
After the scan, write the two headers once:
\[
\mathsf W[b_{\mathbb W}^{\rm out}]\gets K,\qquad\mathsf W[b_{\mathbb W}^{\rm out}+1]\gets\mathsf W[\zeta_\iota+c(v_{\rm out})-1].
\]
Unused parent fields cause no map lookup. Each record requires at most two parent-label reads and one sorting comparison. All scan reads, map and output writes, comparisons, address calculations, and loop updates are charged to $W_{\rm scan}$. Bijectivity of $\iota$ gives $4K$ distinct word-field cells and $K$ distinct real-field cells, with the two headers outside the word-field range. Hence
\[
W_{\rm scan}\le C(3K+1)\le CK,\qquad\operatorname{OutputStorage}=4K+2+K=5K+2.
\]

With $A_0=1$, compute the safe point and embed $q$ by
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_i&=A_{i-1}+\begin{cases}X_{i,1},&X_{i,1}\ge0,\\-X_{i,1},&X_{i,1}<0,\end{cases}\qquad(i\in[N]),\\
a_j&=\begin{cases}A_N,&j=1,\\0,&2\le j\le d,\end{cases}\\
q_{\mathbb R}=\mathsf R[32]&\gets\operatorname{embed}(\mathsf W[r_*+1]),\qquad W_a\le C(N+d).
\end{aligned}
\]
The gate parameters in~\eqref{eq:compiler-parameters} use fixed rational literals, input reads, $+,-,\times$, sign tests, and the displayed embedding. After computing $a$, each parameter costs $W_{\lambda(v)}\le C$; neither $D$ nor a power, exponential, or logarithm is evaluated.

Let $L_*$ be the largest fixed word literal. Evaluate word expressions first in $\mathbb N$, guarding each subtraction by its lower index bound. For the set $\mathcal W$ of all word-register values, addresses, counters, and intermediate word-arithmetic results,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:compiler-ram-capacity}
\begin{aligned}
0&\le(i-1)L\le H_0-L,\qquad 0\le4(k-1)+j<4K_0,\qquad 0\le2j+1<4H_0,\\
\max\mathcal W&\le\max\{q,L_*,4000H_0\},\qquad C_{\rm mem}(d,s)\ge4000L+L_*+1,\\
\max\mathcal W&<q+C_{\rm mem}(d,s)(N+1)<2^w.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Thus word arithmetic agrees with arithmetic in $\mathbb N$, and all addresses are available. The constant $C_{\rm mem}$ is not a program literal. The construction therefore defines a finite program $\mathcal P_{d,s}$ implementing the emitters and scans, whose fixed instructions and literals depend only on $d,s$.

name: Nonanalyticity of the finite-set Parusi\'nski-Rainer extension

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $K\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\bigcup_{a\in\mathbb X}\overline{B(a,1)}$. We first prove that the finite-set recursion produces an extension supported in $K$. More precisely, for $S\subseteq\mathbb X$ and an input jet $\mathcal J=(J^\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le s}$, where $J^\alpha:\mathbb X\to\mathbb{R}$ and $J^\alpha|_{\mathbb X\setminus S}=0$, we prove this assertion by induction on $|S|$, with $S$ as the auxiliary support set in that recursion. If $\mathcal J=0$, the construction returns zero; this includes the case $S=\varnothing$.

Suppose $|S|\ge1$ and that the assertion holds for smaller auxiliary support sets. Let $a\in S$ be the first point selected by the recursion and put $A\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\mathbb X\setminus(S\setminus\{a\})$. Then $J^\alpha|_{A\setminus\{a\}}=0$ for $|\alpha|\le s$. The one-point construction in~\cite[Lemma~4.1, p.~335]{ParusinskiRainer2024}, applied to $\mathcal J|_A$, uses $r\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\min(\{1\}\cup\{|a-b|:b\in A\setminus\{a\}\})\in(0,1]$ and the function
\[
h(x)\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\chi\!\left(\frac{x-a}{r}\right)\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\frac{J^\alpha(a)}{\alpha!}(x-a)^\alpha,\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^d,
\]
where $\chi\in C^{s+1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ is the cutoff used in the construction, with $\chi=1$ near $0$ and $\operatorname{supp}\chi\subset B(0,1)$. The formula also gives $h=0$ if $\mathcal J|_A=0$. Since $\operatorname{supp}h\subseteq a+r\operatorname{supp}\chi\subset B(a,r)$ and $r\le|a-b|$ for $b\in A\setminus\{a\}$, the function $h$ vanishes on a neighborhood of each such $b$. At $a$, the cutoff is identically one on a neighborhood. Consequently, for every $|\alpha|\le s$,
\[
\partial^\alpha h(b)=J^\alpha(b)\quad(b\in A),\qquad \widetilde J^\alpha\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} J^\alpha-\partial^\alpha h|_{\mathbb X},\qquad \widetilde J^\alpha|_{\mathbb X\setminus(S\setminus\{a\})}=0.
\]
By~\cite[proof of Theorem~1.3, p.~336]{ParusinskiRainer2024}, the recursion returns $u=h+\widetilde u$, where $\widetilde u$ is the recursively constructed extension of $(\widetilde J^\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le s}$ with auxiliary support set $S\setminus\{a\}$. The induction hypothesis gives $\operatorname{supp}\widetilde u\subseteq K$, and hence $\operatorname{supp}u\subseteq\operatorname{supp}h\cup\operatorname{supp}\widetilde u\subseteq\overline{B(a,1)}\cup K=K$. This closes the induction. Applied to the prescribed jet, it yields $\operatorname{supp}f\subseteq K$; the set $K$ is compact because $\mathbb X$ is finite.

Suppose now that $f|_U\in C^\omega(U)$, and fix $x\in U$. Choose a unit vector $v$ outside the finite set $\{\pm(a-x)/|a-x|:a\in\mathbb X\}$; such a choice is possible because $d\ge2$. Then $(x+\mathbb{R} v)\cap\mathbb X=\varnothing$, so $g(t)\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} f(x+tv)$ is real-analytic on $\mathbb{R}$. Choose $R>0$ with $K\subset B(0,R)$. For $|t|>R+|x|$, the inequality $|x+tv|\ge|t|-|x|>R$ gives $g(t)=0$. Thus $Z\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}\bigcap_{j=0}^{\infty}(g^{(j)})^{-1}(\{0\})$ is nonempty and closed. For each $t_0\in Z$, real analyticity supplies $\varepsilon>0$ such that $g(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}g^{(j)}(t_0)(t-t_0)^j/j!=0$ whenever $|t-t_0|<\varepsilon$. All derivatives of $g$ therefore vanish on this interval, proving that $Z$ is open. Connectedness of $\mathbb{R}$ yields $Z=\mathbb{R}$, and hence $f(x)=g(0)=0$. Since $x$ was arbitrary, $f$ vanishes on $U$; continuity and finiteness of $\mathbb X$ then give $f\equiv0$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$. In particular, $\partial^\alpha f(a)=0$ for every $a\in\mathbb X$ and $|\alpha|\le s$, contradicting interpolation of the prescribed nonzero jet.
